articles.title: Nier: Automata Dev Working on Fix for Patch That Accidentally Bloated the Game Size to 366GB on PC
articles.summary: Nier: Automata got a patch yesterday to add support for more languages to the game (Korean, Simplified Chinese, and Traditional Chinese), but it accidentally bloated the game file size to 366GB on PC. That’s 1.5 copies of GTA 6!
body: A bug caused the entire game to be applied to every DLC pack included in the PC edition, ballooning the overall file size to Call of Duty-esque heights. Nier was previously around 50GB to download.
The game saw a wave of negative reviews come in on Steam following the patch, with players complaining that they were unable to play or, you know, download any other games.

"Claude, please add new language support for my game, no mistakes, masterpiece. It's 366 gigabytes now? Splendid,” said one review, making a joke about Square Enix using AI. “Undeniably good game which I've had to remove from my computer because some genius, presumably misusing automated tools, packed it into itself six times over, making a 360 gig install file. I'll recommend this game after it is fixed,” said another.

“I think the funniest part about the ‘slight’ issue with the new update for language support is the Steam page still lists a 50gb storage requirement. Good one guys,” reads another negative review. “Played this on PS4 loved it but 366GB is unacceptable for a company like them... fix this Square or I will STOP my FF14 sub,” read another.
points: Nier: Automata got a patch yesterday to add support for more languages to the game (Korean, Simplified Chinese, and Traditional Chinese), but it accidentally bloated the game file size to 366GB on PC.

articles.title: Pilot Draws Incredible GTA 6 Mural With His Flight Path
articles.summary: Benjamin McDaniel, who calls himself The Pilot Picasso, just unveiled his new masterpiece: a GTA 6 mural drawn by flying his plane. Using flight path visualization systems, you can watch his entire journey and see the artwork come to life.
body: It’s kind of like an Etch A Sketch because it’s a continuous line from start to finish, which is part of what makes the feat so impressive. The other thing that makes it impressive is, you know, he kept the plane in the sky the entire time.
The artwork showed the GTA 6 logo next to an alligator, palm trees, a sports car, and a bikini clad woman. A helicopter hovered above the logo.

His upcoming projects include a classical piece and a Thanksgiving piece. In a recent interview, he said, “Safety is number one. If bad weather rolls around, I push the flight to another day or another week.”

In October, The Pilot Picasso flew a route that traced out the Mona Lisa, and previously he also flew Edvard Munch’s The Scream. Previous pop culture artworks include The Lord of The Rings, Skyrim, and Spider-Man.

articles.title: It's Official: The PlayStation Blackout Protest Did Nothing
articles.summary: Disgruntled players tried to boycott Sony in August after the company announced it would discontinue physical media. However, it seems that the PlayStation Digital Blackout protest was a bust.
body: With Sony ceasing disc production in January 2028 and allegedly trying to establish a digital game monopoly, PlayStation owners who were unhappy with its recent business practices organized a boycott. From Aug. 23 until Aug. 30, participants pledged not to make in-game purchases, buy digital games, or renew PlayStation Plus subscriptions. However, the protest gained less traction than expected. Circana's video game industry advisor, Mat Piscatella, initially noted that there hadn't been any significant change in player count or engagement during the blackout.

The financial records have confirmed the protest's insignificance to Sony's business. Not only did sales and engagement not go down, but they actually went up, with Insomniac Games' Marvel's Wolverine leading the charge with 2.4 million units sold. Compared to the previous quarter, monthly active users increased by 2 million and digital sales rose by ¥138.8 billion — ¥158.7 billion if you count add-ons, which is about $996.2 million, using FYQ2's average conversion rate.
points: Disgruntled players tried to boycott Sony in August after the company announced it would discontinue physical media.
However, it seems that the PlayStation Digital Blackout protest was a bust.

articles.title: After Buying EA, Silver Lake and PIF Are Reportedly Now Seeking to Acquire Gaming Software Provider Unity
articles.summary: A consortium of investors including private equity firm Silver Lake Partners and Saudi Arabia’s sovereign wealth fund PIF has held recent talks to acquire gaming software provider Unity.
body: A Reuters report citing confidential sources familiar with the matter states that PIF and Silver Lake, the latter of which already owns 8% of Unity, approached the company in recent weeks. The buyer consortium discussed a valuation of about $25 billion before Unity’s latest earnings report, which lifted its market capitalization to roughly $21.5 billion.
Unity has reportedly been consulting with an investment bank to evaluate its options following the approach, however talks are preliminary and no deal is assured.

Should the acquisition go ahead, this would be another major investment into the games industry for Silver Lake and PIF. The two firms previously teamed up with Jared Kushner’s Affinity Partners to acquire Electronic Arts for $55 billion in a deal that was finalised in August. Since then the publisher has initiated major corporate restructurings and studio closures, most recently shutting development studio BioWare and cancelling the next Mass Effect game.

articles.title: Zelda: Ocarina of Time Producer Doesn’t Want Nintendo’s Next Generation To Rely on BotW’s Ideas
articles.summary: Nintendo’s Legend of Zelda series has remained relevant for 40 years, a streak that the Switch 2’s new Ocarina of Time remake is already set to continue. If you’re looking to understand how a game series stays fresh for four decades, part of that answer can be found in the series’ constant…
body: In an interview with Polygon, producer Hidemaro Fujibayashi explained why Zelda games tend to change rather than stick to one formula. For the series’ producers, a lot of it comes down to the creative freedom that gives the series a natural "malleability," according to Fujibayashi.

That philosophy is currently top of mind for Fujibayashi as the Zelda series enters a new era. For Ocarina of Time, the series’ long-time producers worked with many fresh developers, some of whom weren’t very familiar with the original game. When working with those developers, Fujibayashi said that he encourages the team not to simply take notes from previous games.

“A lot of times, the question I have when I talk to younger staff is like, ‘Is that going to be fun?’” Fujibayashi said. “Or I would say sometimes, ‘Well, I think we did that in Breath of the Wild. I think we touched that on Tears of Kingdom. I feel like I saw it in Ocarina of Time.’ These are just examples, I don't actually directly say that. But this is the kind of probing and discussion that we do with the team such that they don't feel like they need to pull from an already existing pool of ideas that Zelda has plotted.”

articles.title: "Is there any accountability left in this world?" Warren Spector pops off at EA executives and their massive payouts as BioWare shuts down
articles.summary: It's only been two weeks since we last heard Warren Spector sound off about EA's sudden decision to close BioWare, following the publisher's acquisition by Saudi Arabia's PIF and venture capitalist concerns. But now, the storied developer is back and - apparently - angrier than ever.
body: "I recently posted my thoughts about EA’s shuttering of BioWare," Spector wrote in a post on LinkedIn. "Those of you who read my post know that I was unhappy. I remain so. The tragedy of so many layoffs the last few years hasn’t been lost on me, but for some reason, BioWare hit me on an emotional level that nothing before had. I felt gut-punched."

Spector goes on to counter the idea that the studio was closed down as a "sound business decision" because the "studio’s glory days (artistic and commercial) were behind them" and that "businesses don’t succeed on history alone". These reactions, more than anything else, appear to be what's inspired Spector to take to posting again - he simply cannot agree with this assessment.

"If studio-level people leave, resulting in dilution of talent, someone is creating an environment that pushes them out. Do those culture-killers pay any price? If executives misread the market, over-hire, or make decisions that result in under-funded, over-funded, poorly-marketed games do they lose sleep let alone jobs?" he asks.

articles.title: After gobbling up EA, Saudi Arabia and private equity firm Silver Lake reportedly looking to buy Unity
articles.summary: After acquiring EA for $55bn earlier this year, Saudi Arabia and private equity firm Silver Lake are reportedly in the market for another massive video game company. And according to new reports, it's Unity.
body: Per Reuters, Saudi Arabia's Public Investment Fund (PIF) and Silver Lake - two major actors in the EA acquisition - are in talks to acquire the video game engine company for around $25bn. Silver Lake's Egon Durban already sits on the Unity Board of Directors, and the firm owns around eight percent of its shares already thanks to a $400m investment.

This $25bn valuation should be taken with a grain of salt for two core reasons. For one, it was decided prior to Unity's latest quarterly financial report, which included a 59% increase in strategic revenue year-over-year and net income of $122m. So this could propel the valuation upwards.

On the other hand, wider economic changes could have a detrimental effect. Reuters points out: "Strong ⁠growth in Unity's AI-powered Vector advertising platform helped it post its first quarterly profit on a GAAP basis since going public in September 2020." Given we've seen the generative AI sector take a major hit this week following the US midterm elections, it's possible companies using the tech may be viewed with more fiscal skepticism. Or, maybe this dip is just temporary. In short, take the $25bn valuation as a ballpark figure.
points: After acquiring EA for $55bn earlier this year, Saudi Arabia and private equity firm Silver Lake are reportedly in the market for another massive video game company.

articles.title: Tim Burton's Forgotten 10/10 Fantasy Masterpiece is Officially Still Free on Streaming
articles.summary: When the conversation turns to Tim Burton ’s best movies, the same titles tend to surface: Beetlejuice, his Batman movies, Edward Scissorhands, Ed Wood, and Pee-Wee’s Big Adventure. Even The Nightmare Before Christmas usually gets a mention, despite being directed by Henry Selick.
body: Big Fish follows Will Bloom (Billy Crudup), a man trying to reconnect with his semi-estranged, dying father, Edward (Albert Finney). Edward has spent a lifetime telling stories about his younger self, played by Ewan McGregor in a series of elaborate flashbacks. His adventures involve an 11-foot-tall giant, conjoined twin singers, and a seven-foot-long catfish. Will has heard them all before. What he wants, while there’s still time, is to meet the man behind the tall tales.

That tension gives Big Fish its emotional weight, but the movie’s immediate appeal is its charm. Much of that comes from the two actors playing Edward. McGregor and Finney don’t particularly resemble each other, yet they’re completely convincing as the same man at opposite ends of his life.

articles.title: Remakes and new games "both have a place in the stable" says Nintendo boss, buoyed by the success of Star Fox and Ocarina of Time
articles.summary: It's been a good year for Nintendo: between Star Fox - the N64 classic with a dazzling facelift on Switch 2 - and the newly-launched and utterly fantastic Ocarina of Time remake, the platform holder is having a good run.
body: As popular as its other games are, though, you have to admit that 2026 has been a banner year for Nintendo's remakes - both Star Fox and Ocarina of Time have commanded plenty of headline-grabbing attention over the past 12 months, and it's a fact that isn't lost on the company. In a new interview with Polygon, Nintendo's Nate Bihldorff - senior vice president of product development and publishing - says that wholly new games and remakes of classics are of "equal importance" to the publisher going forward.

There's more interesting stuff in the interview, as Bihldorff outlines his views on the strenght of the Nintendo roster - "it doesn't matter how excited I am about Donkey Kong Bananza at launch; there's always going to be more games that are coming down the pipeline" - and that the release pipeline continues to look as strong for the Switch 2 as it did for the Switch. "There's one constant that has been consistent through my entire career at Nintendo, and that's that you can pretty much set your watch by the idea that we're going to be coming out with stuff," Bihldorff told Polygon.

articles.title: WoW: Forever is working on its server tech to make cities less empty, say devs
articles.summary: World of Warcraft: Forever 's launch has been downright impressive—MMOs are notoriously difficult to run servers for, particularly when it comes to launch, where players will get bottlenecked into servers, throwing devs into a catch 22: Do they increase capacity and wind up wasting money in the…
body: Which is why I'm willing to forgive Blizzard for a weird quirk of its realmless layering technology—cities have been empty, empty as hell. Which is a shame, given I know that hundreds of thousands of players are technically on this thing—and yet, none of them are in my Stormwind.

Well, Forever's devs are working on a fix, per the official forums: "Just wanted to chime in," says Aggrend, "And say that we are aware of some issues with certain areas not feeling as populated as they should. We will be tweaking some numbers tomorrow to help things feel a bit more lively. Thanks for the feedback on this one!"

That's a relief to hear, especially given I'm on a roleplay server, and there have been problems with this sort of thing where phasing has interrupted the flow of narrative commerce in the past. Cities, especially, should feel lived-in, and it's hard to create a sense of community when people you could be writing with keep bamfing in and out of existence.

articles.title: "It's a brave new world": GTA 6's PC port will release sooner than you think to avoid losing money to AI rip-offs, says former Rockstar tech director
articles.summary: GTA 6 's PC release may come sooner than anticipated, according to former Rockstar North technical director Obbe Vermeij, because Rockstar and publishers Take-Two will be concerned about losing money to unofficial generative AI clones of the PS5 version, once it launches on 19th November.
body: Speaking to me during a wide-ranging chatathon, Vermeij reflected on the early days of Grand Theft Auto development at Rockstar North in the 90s, and how the Noel-and-Liam-Gallagher-esque relationship between PC and console gaming has evolved. He shared a sweary anecdote about the company's difficulties getting the original GTA 1 to look the business on Sony's PlayStation.

"I didn't work on GTA 1 and 2, but I worked for the company at the time, and I was actually right next to the GTA 1 team, so I was able to follow it," he said. "So they worked on PC and then an external company in Dundee did the PlayStation version. Which was really weird, because like, PCs were so much more powerful - still the case, but in those days, it was even more so.

articles.title: Amazon Reveals Free Uber Eats Delivery for Prime Members, Plus $20 Off Your First Two Orders
articles.summary: Amazon Prime members can now get $0 delivery fees on orders over $25. Amazon revealed in a November 5 press release that this benefit is now available to use, and subscribers are eligible for $20 off their first two orders for the next two weeks.
body: This new service replaces the Prime GrubHub+ benefit, which has officially expired as of today. If you're already a member, all you need to do is search 'Uber Eats' on Amazon to find restaurants and start placing an order. Alternatively, you can go straight to the official Uber Eats page to check out what's available.

The press release doesn't explain why Amazon made the shift from GrubHub+ to Uber Eats, only that this will be the partnership moving forward. Amazon Prime Vice President Jamil Ghani commented on how the deal fits into the service, saying: “This is what Prime is all about: unlimited free, fast delivery on a wide selection of products, big savings, fantastic entertainment, and now even more value on restaurant delivery with Uber Eats, all in a single membership.”

For those with an Amazon Prime membership already, this is basically free food money. You can use this promotion to get a discount on dinner for your family or go wild and order a stack of KFC Doomsday Chicken Sandwiches for yourself. The bonus $20 off credit will only last from now until November 18.

articles.title: EA Killed Mass Effect But Is Still Trying To Make Money On It
articles.summary: Electronic Arts recently killed off Mass Effect and closed developer BioWare entirely, but the publisher is still trying to make money from the franchise's fanbase. Ahead of the annual Mass Effect holiday of N7 Day on November 7, EA is promoting Mass Effect via posts about what fans can buy on the…
body: The BioWare Gear Store's social media presence came back to life after a month of darkness today to start hawking Mass Effect merch. The post that kicked things off is the one below, in which fans are invited to "celebrate the legacy" of Mass Effect by giving EA money.
EA followed the post up with eight more, pushing people to visit the BioWare Gear Store to buy things like mugs, tote bags, clothing, and shoes, among other things.
The replies under every one of the posts call out how cold and gross it is to promote the brand so soon after cancelling Mass Effect 5 and closing BioWare.

EA made the drastic changes as part of a big organizational shift and wider pullback that also included layoffs and other game cancellations, like a new The Sims game. These moves came after EA was taken private by an investor consortium led by Saudi Arabia's Public Investment Fund in a deal that included billions of debt.

articles.title: 49 Years Later, Steven Spielberg’s Sci-Fi Thriller Masterpiece Is Officially Free on YouTube
articles.summary: Most creators are lucky if they ever make one truly revolutionary thing in their lives. Steven Spielberg has made at least six.
body: He's had his misfires and genuine failures along the way, but Spielberg has reshaped multiple genres and filmmaking as a whole in his wake. Many of his movies have become part of the bedrock of worldwide culture. There are multiple different trends and revivals that can be traced straight back to Spielberg, from Indiana Jones' faux-serial period action to Saving Private Ryan redefining war films to virtually every monster movie made after 1975.

In retrospect, however, there's one entertainment subgenre that we might not give Spielberg enough credit for, and that's the alien conspiracy thriller. 1977's Close Encounters of the Third Kind was Spielberg's second big hit after Jaws. While it hasn't latched onto the popular imagination in quite the way that some of Spielberg's later films did, it's hard not to see Close Encounters' influence on the subsequent alien-abduction films and TV of the 1980s and 1990s.
